description: A six-panel composite of secondary-electron SEM micrographs (each annotated 20kV) showing nano-sized carbides formed by spinodal decomposition in Fe–Mn–Al–C lightweight steels at 800 °C. Panels are laid out as three alloy rows × two magnifications: the left column (a, c, e) is ×10,000 with a 1 µm scale bar, the right column (b, d, f) is ×30,000 with a 0.5 µm scale bar. (a, b) 9Al-10Mn-1C: a grid of thin, interwoven acicular needle-like precipitates of medium density; (a) additionally shows a large smooth region carrying dark plate-like particles above the fine precipitate grid. (c, d) 12Al-20Mn-1C: the densest and thickest precipitate array, with proper cuboidal morphology forming an orthogonal checkerboard grid, separated from a second oriented region by a boundary. (e, f) 12Al-30Mn-1C: carbides agglomerated again into acicular-like precipitates, in (e) surrounding large bright blocky islands, and in (f) appearing as the finest and least dense network. Scale bars and magnification text are printed in every panel; no numerical property values are printed.

subfigures.description: SE-SEM micrograph, 20kV, ×10,000, 1 µm scale bar. Dense grid of thin acicular/needle-like precipitates in a matrix, with a large smooth featureless region at top-left containing dark plate-like particles.
SE-SEM micrograph, 20kV, ×30,000, 0.5 µm scale bar. Higher magnification of the acicular precipitate grid, showing interwoven needle-like carbides of medium density.
SE-SEM micrograph, 20kV, ×10,000, 1 µm scale bar. Very dense, thick cuboidal precipitates forming an orthogonal checkerboard pattern; two differently oriented regions meet along a boundary.
SE-SEM micrograph, 20kV, ×30,000, 0.5 µm scale bar. Higher magnification of the cuboidal precipitate array, showing the thickest and densest configuration of the three alloys.
SE-SEM micrograph, 20kV, ×10,000, 1 µm scale bar. Agglomerated acicular precipitates surrounding large bright blocky islands, at lower precipitate density than (a) and (c).
SE-SEM micrograph, 20kV, ×30,000, 0.5 µm scale bar. Fine, sparsely distributed acicular carbide network; the least dense of the three ×30,000 views.

observations.observation: The group is a 3 × 2 array of SEM micrographs: left column (a, c, e) at ×10,000 with a 1 µm scale bar, right column (b, d, f) at ×30,000 with a 0.5 µm scale bar, all labelled 20kV.
Panels (a) and (b) show thin, interwoven acicular (needle-like) carbides arranged in a medium-density grid.
In 9Al-10Mn-1C, carbides agglomerated into thin acicular morphologies in a relatively medium-dense grid (Fig. 8(a), (b)).
Panels (c) and (d) show a dense array of thick, cuboidal precipitates forming an orthogonal checkerboard grid.
In 12Al-20Mn-1C, carbides presented the densest and thickest configuration with proper cuboidal morphology (Fig. 8(c), (d)).
Panel (e) contains large bright blocky islands (grain-boundary-scale features) surrounded by agglomerated acicular precipitates.
In 12Al-30Mn-1C, carbides agglomerated again into acicular-like precipitates, but with the finest and less dense configuration (Fig. 8(e), (f)).
Panel (f) shows the sparsest and finest acicular carbide network among the three ×30,000 micrographs (b), (d) and (f).
The caption states the carbides are nano-sized and were produced from spinodal decomposition in 9Al-10Mn-1C, 12Al-20Mn-1C and 12Al-30Mn-1C at 800 °C.
Panel (a) contains a large smooth, featureless region with dark plate-like particles that is distinct from the fine precipitate grid occupying the rest of the field.

No numeric composition, hardness or precipitate-size value is printed inside any panel; the only printed quantities are the 20kV voltage, the ×10,000/×30,000 magnifications and the 1 µm / 0.5 µm scale bars.

unreadable_items: The Greek kappa symbol in the caption and citing sentences is rendered as '--carbides'; the phase symbol itself cannot be read from the figure text, though the context indicates κ-carbide
Composition units (wt.% vs at.%) for the alloy labels 9Al-10Mn-1C etc. are not stated in the figure
